chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the dowry, meaning in al-Mut'ah (temporary marriage)?' He said: 'Whatever they agree upon for whatever duration they choose.' I said: 'What do you think if she becomes pregnant?' He said: 'The child is his.' If he wishes to enter into a new matter, he may do so, and there is no waiting period for her from him. And from another man, she has five and forty nights. And if they stipulate inheritance, then they are upon their stipulation.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: Waiting period after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for dowry, duration, and waiting period in Shia temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Ishtibār, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the dowry and duration of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) are entirely subject to mutual consent, highlighting the contractual flexibility unique to this institution. The hadith further establishes that the child’s lineage is attributed to the husband and that the wife’s waiting period ('Iddah) is determined by pregnancy or the standard five months and twenty days, while explicitly validating the stipulation of inheritance rights between the parties. This ruling underscores the legal autonomy granted to spouses in Mut'ah, distinguishing it from permanent marriage in terms of inheritance and contractual conditions.
